content_html:
Embedded Memory Mechanisms in Plants & Animals

Both plants and animals implement embedded memory: experiences change the substrate (chromatin/tissues vs synapses/circuits), biasing future responses.

  • Mechanistic substrates differ, but the logic is conserved: experience leaves a trace that biases future computation/behavior.
  • Plant electrical signaling can propagate action‑potential‑like events along vasculature, coordinating systemic responses.
Theme Plants Animals
Physical medium Chromatin marks; signaling pathway states; tissue architecture Synaptic weights; spine morphology; network connectivity
Short-term change Priming via Ca²⁺/ROS/hormone sensitivity Short-term plasticity; neuromodulators
Long-term change Stable epigenetic marks; structural remodeling; vernalization LTP/LTD; dendritic remodelling; systems consolidation
System-wide integration Electrical/chemical signals via phloem/xylem; SAR Neural/electrical signals via circuits; endocrine/autonomic
Inheritance Transgenerational stress memory reported Developmental programming; cultural/behavioral transmission
